CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  December 10, 2024

The City of Signal Hill appreciates your attendance. Citizen interest provides the Council and
Agency with valuable information regarding issues of the community. Meetings are held on
the 2nd and 4th Tuesday of every month.

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view the meeting live at 6:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  • Charter Spectrum Channel 74 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
To participate during the regular meeting at 6:00 p.m.:

  • In-person Participation: Council Chamber of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 4:00 p.m. on Tuesday, December 10, 2024.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.

  The newly elected members of the City Council and the City Clerk will be sworn

(9)  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  a.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  Summary:

  At the first regular City Council meeting following a general municipal election,
  newly elected Council Members are sworn and seated. The City Council shall
  designate one of its members as Mayor and one of its members as Vice Mayor,
  at the first regular City Council meeting following the anniversary of that date for
  any year in which no general municipal election is held.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. Reorganize by selecting a new Mayor and Vice Mayor.
  2. The newly appointed Mayor will present a proclamation to outgoing Mayor
  Woods.

(10)  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  a.  PUBLIC HEARING - RESOLUTION APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE OF
  FISCAL YEAR (FY) 2025-26 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT
  (CDBG) FUNDS

  Summary:

  The City Council will conduct a public hearing and consider proposed uses for
  the City’s FY 2025-26 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funding
  allocation. The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA) estimates
  the City will receive approximately $70,146 to use on CDBG projects and
  programs.

  Staff is proposing to allocate the funding for the continuation of the City’s Food
  Distribution programs and the construction of Americans with Disabilities Act
  (ADA) ramps and sidewalk improvements. If approved, the City Council is
  required to adopt a resolution affirming the use of CDBG funds for the projects.

  Form of Notice: Notice was published in the Signal Tribune newspaper per
  Government Code Section 65091(a)(4) and posted in accordance with the
  Signal Hill Municipal Code Section 1.08.010 on Friday, November 22, 2024.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. Adopt the following resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL
  HILL, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING THE CITY'S PROPOSED
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT PROGRAMS FOR
  FISCAL YEAR 2025-26

  2. Approve the CDBG estimated allocation for FY 2025-26 in the amount of
  $70,146 and the proposed expenditures of these allocations.
(11)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

  a.  ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2023-24

  Page 4 of 18
 City Council  Regular  December 10, 2024

  Summary:

  The Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) is an independently
  audited summary report of the City’s financial transactions for Fiscal Year (FY)
  2023-24. The ACFR provides relevant financial information to the City Council,
  residents, current and future employees, grant entities, creditors, bond investors,
  rating agencies, and other interested parties. The audit is performed in
  compliance with the requirements of the City Charter, and the results are
  presented to the City Council for review.

  The audit was completed by the City's independent auditor, Rogers, Anderson,
  Malody & Scott, LLP, Certified Public Accountants (RAMS), which issued an
  unqualified opinion audit report, otherwise known as a “clean opinion” finding
  nothing of material concern in the City’s internal controls, financial, and
  bookkeeping practices. The independent auditor’s unmodified report provides
  assurance that the ACFR, and audited information within, present fairly the
  City’s financial position for the Fiscal Year ending June 30, 2024.

  As part of the ACFR, staff provides detailed information and recommendations
  regarding the General Fund Operating balance. For FY 2023-24 the General
  Fund reports a positive fund balance of $11.1 million. Staff will present
  recommendations for fund balance appropriations to the City Council in the first
  part of the 2025 calendar year. This proposed timeline allows staff to conduct a
  detailed analysis of the positive fund balance, including ongoing revenue
  updates, requests to re-appropriate unutilized budget appropriations, one-time
  expenditure requests for department operations, programs or special projects,
  and reserve allocations resulting in budget adjustments for the current fiscal
  year.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1 Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability and
  resilience.
  Recommendations:

  1. Receive and file the City’s ACFR for FY 2023-24.

  2. Direct staff to return the first part of the 2025 calendar year with proposed
  appropriations for the FY 2023-24 General Fund positive fund balance.

  3. Direct staff to distribute copies of the ACFR for FY 2023-24 as required, as
  well as to the Office of the City Clerk to be placed on file for the general public
  and posted on the City’s website.
  b.  WATER MASTER PLAN AND RATE STUDY SUBCOMMITTEE FORMATION

  Summary:

  Page 5 of 18
 City Council  Regular  December 10, 2024

  The City of Signal Hill’s 2023-2028 Strategic Plan identifies conducting a
  comprehensive water rate study and updating the Water Master Plan (WMP) to
  ensure the sustained delivery of safe and clean water while enhancing financial
  sustainability as key initiatives.

  The City’s Water rates, last adopted in 2019, established rates for the period
  from 2020 to 2024. On December 7, 2023, the City Council approved a
  consulting services agreement with Dudek Engineering Services (Dudek) to
  prepare the Water Master Plan and Water Rate Study Project.

  Currently, the City is in the process of updating both the WMP and the Water
  Rate Study (WRS). The WMP assesses the City's water system infrastructure,
  identifies deficiencies, and outlines a strategic plan for capital improvements
  over the next five years. Building on the findings of the WMP, the WRS aims to
  establish a sustainable and equitable rate structure to ensure adequate funding
  for operations and capital projects.

  Staff is recommending to appoint two council members to serve on a
  subcommittee to review the preliminary financial analysis, provide guidance on
  findings, and develop recommendations for rate adjustments. If approved, staff
  would schedule the subcommittee meeting for either Tuesday, December 17,
  2024 or Monday, January 27, 2025; a Water Rate Study Council Workshop at
  the City Council meeting of Tuesday, February 25, 2025; and a Water Rate
  Study Community Workshop on Monday, March 10, 2025.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendations:

  1. Appoint two City Council members to serve on a subcommittee to review the
  Water Master Plan preliminary financial analysis and develop
  recommendations for any necessary water rate adjustments.

  2. Select one of the following dates for the subcommittee meeting: Tuesday,
  December 17, 2024 or Monday, January 27, 2025.

  3. Schedule the Water Rate Study Council Meeting Workshop for Tuesday,

  Page 6 of 18
 City Council  Regular  December 10, 2024

  February 25, 2025.

  4. Schedule the Water Rate Study Community Workshop for Monday, March 10,
  2025.

  b.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2024-11-1551 APPROVING ZONING
  ORDINANCE AMENDMENT 24-01, AMENDING THE OFFICIAL ZONING MAP
  TO CHANGE AN APPROXIMATE 0.59-ACRE SITE AT 1933 THROUGH 1939
  TEMPLE AVENUE FROM RESIDENTIAL HIGH DENSITY (RH) TO THE
  COURTYARD SPECIFIC PLAN (SP-21) AND ADDING CHAPTER 20.28, THE
  COURTYARD SPECIFIC PLAN (SP-21) TO THE SIGNAL HILL MUNICIPAL
  CODE AND ESTABLISHING DEVELOPMENT STANDARDS FOR THE SITE

  Summary:

  The City Council introduced Ordinance No. 2024-11-1551 at its regular meeting
  on Tuesday, November 12, 2024. The Signal Hill City Council approved Zoning
  Ordinance Amendment 24-01, changing the zoning of a 0.59-acre site at
  1933-1939 Temple Avenue from Residential High Density (RH) to the Courtyard
  Specific Plan (SP-21). This ordinance also adds Chapter 20.28 to the Municipal
  Code, establishing development standards for the site under the Courtyard
  Specific Plan.

  Staff prepared the Ordinance for second reading and adoption.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  downtown core.

  e.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A BUDGET AMENDMENT FOR THE
  PROCUREMENT OF A POLICE DEPARTMENT COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT
  VEHICLE

  Summary:

  The Signal Hill Police Department is seeking approval for a budget amendment
  to procure a fully customized, 4x4 off-road Community Engagement Vehicle. If
  approved, the Community Engagement Vehicle would be used at citywide
  community events such as National Night Out and recruitment fairs. The
  proposed Community Engagement Vehicle’s primary purpose is to strengthen
  communication between officers and the public, supporting the Police
  Department’s community policing and recruitment efforts. The vehicle’s compact
  size and ability to be customized with branding, make it an effective tool to
  capture public interest and build rapport with the Signal Hill community.

  The City Council will consider the approval of the proposed community
  engagement vehicle, and corresponding budget adjustment. Staff has identified
  that the vehicle make, model, and requested specifications is exclusively
  available at a single dealership in Southern California. In compliance with the
  City’s purchasing policy, the vendor has provided a sole source letter. The
  Police Department has also negotiated preferred pricing for a 2025 model
  vehicle. As a result, the timing of the City’s budget adjustment request is critical
  to securing the vehicle at the promotional rate.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND AUTHORIZING
  BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025
  f.  PROPOSED ACCEPTANCE OF OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY SELECTIVE
  TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM GRANT AND ADOPTION OF
  RESOLUTION APPROVING BUDGET AMENDMENT

  Summary:

  Page 10 of 18
 City Council  Regular  December 10, 2024

  The Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) Selective Traffic Enforcement Program
  (STEP) awarded the Signal Hill Police Department a grant in the amount of
  $100,000, which is $10,000 more than originally budgeted. The STEP grant
  funding would allow the Police Department to carry out traffic safety
  enforcement, targeting primary collision factors including driving under the
  influence. If accepted, the grant would help offset the cost of staff overtime,
  training, and related supplies. Staff recommends the City Council adopt a
  resolution accepting the grant and authorizing a budget adjustment to increase
  the grant revenue by $10,000.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the Police Chief to accept grant funding through the OTS STEP
  grant.

  2. Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  CALIFORNIA AMENDING THE ADOPTED BUDGET AND AUTHORIZING
  BUDGET APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25
  g.  RESOLUTION DECLARING FINAL ACCEPTANCE OF THE ADA CURB RAMP
  INSTALLATION PROJECT PURSUANT TO THE PUBLIC WORKS
  CONTRACT WITH MAJ ENGINEERING

  Summary:

  The ADA Curb Ramp Installation Project is part of the City’s ongoing efforts to
  enhance accessibility by providing ADA-compliant ramps and improving
  sidewalks throughout the City. On July 23, 2024, the City Council awarded a
  contract to MAJ Engineering for the construction of new ADA-compliant curb
  ramps at various locations within the City. This project is partially funded through
  a Community Development Block Grant (CDBG).

  MAJ Engineering completed work for the ADA Curb Ramp Installation Project in
  accordance with the project specifications and to the satisfaction of the Public
  Works Department. Staff recommends the City Council adopt a resolution
  declaring the work performed by MAJ Engineering as complete and in

  conformance with the approved plans and specifications.

  SPECIFICATIONS FOR THE ADA CURB RAMP INSTALLATION PROJECT IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH THE CONTRACT ENTERED INTO BETWEEN MAJ
  ENGINEERING INCORPORATED AND THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  h.  PUBLIC WORKS CONTRACT WITH ESTATE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION
  INCORPORATED FOR THE PANORAMA PROMENADE SLOPE LANDSCAPE
  PROJECT

  Summary:

  In February 2024, the City experienced significant damage to the Panorama
  Promenade and the slope adjacent to Molino Avenue and 20th Street due to
  severe winter storms. In response, the City Council adopted a resolution ratifying
  the City Manager’s proclamation of a local emergency. Subsequently, on
  February 27, 2024, the City Council approved a Public Works contract with
  Zimprich Engineering Incorporated (Zimprich) to carry out emergency repairs for
  the Panorama Promenade Trail and the slope at Molino Avenue and 20th
  Street. The approval included an appropriation of $800,000 from the Fiscal Year
  2023-24 General Fund Unassigned Fund Balance/Capital Improvement Projects
  Reserve to fund the emergency repairs.

  Zimprich successfully completed all emergency repair work at the Panorama
  Promenade Trail and the Molino Avenue and 20th Street slope to the
  satisfaction of the Public Works Department and in compliance with project
  specifications. On October 4, 2024, the City Council adopted a resolution
  declaring final acceptance of the emergency repairs completed by Zimprich
  Engineering.

  During the completion of slope repairs at Panorama Promenade, the Public
  Works Department retained Architerra Design Group (Architerra), the City’s
  on-call contractor, on July 30, 2024, to prepare plans and specifications for
  appropriate seeding, earthwork, and the design of a planting and irrigation
  system. Architerra completed these plans in compliance with geotechnical
  specifications, FEMA planting standards, and City requirements; the finalized
  bid-ready plans were advertised for construction on November 1, 2024, and the
  bid opening took place on November 25, 2024.

  Page 12 of 18
 City Council  Regular  December 10, 2024

  Following a comprehensive and competitive bidding process, the City Council
  will consider awarding a contract to Estate Design and Construction
  Incorporated (EDC), the lowest responsive bidder, for a term of 90 working days
  with a not-to-exceed budget of $297,683.20. The City Council will consider
  authorizing the City Manager to execute a Public Works Contract with EDC, with
  construction scheduled to begin in December 2024 and anticipated completion
  by May 2025.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government Strengthen internal communication,

  effectiveness and efficiency of City services
  Recommendation:

  Panorama Slope Landscape Project, for a term of 90 working days and a
  not-to-exceed contract amount of $297,683.20, in a form approved by the

  Summary:

  Parkwood Landscape Maintenance Incorporated (Parkwood). After review of the
  landscape services provided over the past two annual terms, City staff
  negotiated an amendment to the existing Maintenance Services. The proposed
  Second Amendment would continue the term of the agreement until December
  20, 2025, with an annual not-to-exceed amount of $31,343.66. Staff also
  recommends the City Council authorize a 10% contingency for a total budget for
  the third year of the contract of $34,478.02.

  Page 13 of 18
 City Council  Regular  December 10, 2024

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the proposed Second
  Amendment and authorize the City Manager to sign the agreement with
  Parkwood.

  or any unforeseen conditions, to be utilized if approved by the Public Works

  3. Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING

  APPROPRIATIONS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025
  j.  RESOLUTION AMENDING THE HOURLY PART-TIME SALARY SCHEDULE
  TO COMPLY WITH THE CALIFORNIA STATE MINIMUM WAGE LAW

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider an amendment to the part-time salary resolution
  that would update the City’s hourly, part-time salary ranges to comply with the
  California State minimum wage law. The State’s hourly minimum wage will

  comply with the law. If approved by City Council, the updated salary schedule
  would be effective January 1, 2025.

  RCS Investigations & Consulting, Limited Liability Corporation (RCS) to conduct
  administrative investigations (Internal Affairs Investigations) and background
  investigations for both sworn and non-sworn Signal Hill Police Department
  (Police Department) employees over a five-year term. Since the start of the
  previous contract, the City has executed two amendments to increase the
  not-to-exceed amount and extend the contract term, which was in effect through
  June 30, 2024.

  service agreement would also allow for three one-year extensions with an
